purpose: Test whether a source-fragmented specialist option can still be transformed into a compact structured Foundation layer without whole-topic generation.

coreConcepts: Offender profiling uses behavioural and contextual evidence to infer useful characteristics or patterns relevant to an unknown offender.
A typology-led profiling route starts from pre-existing categories such as organised/disorganised patterns and asks how well the case fits them.
A data-driven route builds inferences from observed crime features, behavioural consistency across offences and empirical patterns rather than beginning with a fixed offender category.
Geographical profiling uses spatial patterns in offence locations to estimate an offender's likely activity base or movement pattern.
Profiling methods are probabilistic investigative aids, not deterministic diagnoses; empirical support and limitations must be evaluated.
structuredKnowledge.alignmentNote: Revision maps the AQA top-down label to typology-led profiling and the bottom-up label to data-driven investigative/geographical methods. The labels are alignment facts; the explanations are independently structured from OPEN evidence.

coreConcepts: Antisocial and criminal behaviour can show measurable genetic influence, but genetic effects are probabilistic rather than deterministic.
Genetic vulnerability operates alongside environmental exposure and developmental context; gene-environment interaction is therefore central to responsible interpretation.
Neurobiological research examines brain structure/function and related biological systems associated with antisocial behaviour.
Biological findings describe risk and association, not an inevitable pathway from biology to offending.
Personality-based explanations link enduring traits to differences in offending risk; Eysenck-style accounts are one historically influential example.
Differential association treats criminal behaviour as learned through interaction with others, including exposure to definitions and norms favourable to offending.
Cognitive explanations examine characteristic ways of interpreting and justifying events, including hostile attribution bias and offence-supportive distortions.
Minimisation and justification can reduce perceived responsibility or harm and form part of offence-supportive cognition.
Moral reasoning accounts examine how judgments about right, wrong, harm and responsibility may relate to offending behaviour.
structuredKnowledge.caution: These are competing/complementary explanations. The Foundation should not collapse personality, learning and cognition into one causal model.

coreConcepts: Custodial sentencing can serve punishment and public-protection purposes while also creating psychological and social consequences for imprisoned people.
Rehabilitation aims to reduce future offending by changing behaviour, skills, cognition or social functioning rather than relying on punishment alone.
Anger-management interventions target recognition and regulation of anger-related responses associated with aggressive behaviour.
Restorative justice focuses on harm, responsibility, victim-offender processes and repair, with outcomes evaluated in relation to both participants and reoffending.
rightsResidual: Behaviour modification/token economy in a custodial/forensic setting: highly relevant 2026 open-access evidence exists, but the exact Creative Commons licence flavour has not been verified as commercially compatible and is therefore not yet reusable corpus evidence.

manualInterventions: reconciliation of psychological and criminal-justice sources
explicit retention of unverified token-economy rights residual

works: A specialist option can still be represented compactly even when evidence comes from many sources rather than one textbook.
Source fragmentation increases search/provenance work but does not necessarily require original subject research.
A narrow rights residual can remain explicit without blocking transformation of the rest of the topic.
prototypeLearning.constraint: The manual effort of finding, licensing and reconciling fragmented specialist sources is now the clearest scalability risk.
prototypeLearning.nextStep: Treat source discovery, licence classification and requirement-to-source mapping as the principal automation opportunity. Keep the token-economy and Prochaska items as explicit unresolved residuals until a commercial-compatible route is established or a deliberate original-content decision is made.
